clue.text: One to arrange publicity for a Clinton?

definitions.text: One to arrange publicity for a Clinton?

blocks.note: surface reading: a press agent or spin doctor working for a politician
setter's reading: Clinton's first name is Bill, and the trade meant is pasting up printed notices called bills

explanation.surface: A spin doctor wonders who handles the image of a member of the Clinton family.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'a Clinton' as Bill Clinton and the answer splits into BILL and POSTER; a billposter is someone who sticks up advertising bills.
explanation.definitionFit: A billposter pastes advertising notices on walls and hoardings, literally spreading publicity in public places.

clue.text: Boring documents etc behind head of finance

indicators.note: the head is the top, so only the first letter of the next word is used

blocks.note: the bum is one's behind, the backside
the first letter

explanation.surface: Tedious paperwork is waiting at the back of the finance director's desk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind' looks like a position word, but it is the noun for the backside. BUMF is British slang for paperwork.
explanation.definitionFit: Bumf is British slang for tedious paperwork, forms and leaflets that nobody wants to read.

clue.text: House in country not finished, crates all over the place

indicators.note: a word left unfinished loses its last letter
things scattered all over the place are jumbled out of order

blocks.note: a country is a land
taken as written

explanation.surface: A country house in chaos while crates lie scattered about during a move.
explanation.walkthrough: House means a royal dynasty, not a building.
explanation.definitionFit: The House of Lancaster was the English royal dynasty that reigned in the fifteenth century, rivals of York.

clue.text: Some housing measure for person responsible for children

indicators.note: something housing another holds it inside, like a building holding a tenant

blocks.note: some of something is a part of it
an en is a printer's unit of measurement

explanation.surface: A housing policy is aimed at those raising children.
explanation.walkthrough: The en is a printing measure, half an em, common in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: A mother or father is the adult who brings up and has responsibility for a child.

clue.text: Renewed energy for playing perhaps but not from top brass

definitions.text: for playing perhaps but not from top brass

blocks.note: first meaning: fresh strength after exhaustion

blocks.clueFragment: for playing perhaps but not from top brass
blocks.note: second meaning, cryptic: an orchestral woodwind player who sits behind the principal, not the leading player

explanation.surface: A fresh burst of energy for a game, though not encouraged by senior officers.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half reads as an orchestra seat: a wind instrumentalist ranked second, not first; 'top brass' hints at the principal players, not army officers.
explanation.definitionFit: A second wind is the revived stamina an athlete feels after initial tiredness passes.

clue.text: With force unused, not so many in jug

indicators.note: a letter left unused is dropped from the word

blocks.note: fewer means not so many
F is the abbreviation for force in physics

explanation.surface: Without using force, not much is going into the jug.
explanation.definitionFit: A ewer is a large wide-mouthed pitcher, traditionally used with a washbasin.

clue.text: Greek characters taking rest-days regularly

indicators.note: at regular intervals, so only every other letter of the following words is kept

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: Greek workers enjoy their days off at regular intervals.
explanation.definitionFit: Eta is the seventh letter of the Greek alphabet, so the plural names several such letters.

clue.text: Pamphlet found in agricultural vehicle or shed

indicators.note: to shed is to cast off, so the little word or goes

blocks.note: the farm vehicle
taken as written

explanation.surface: A leaflet is discovered in a farm vehicle or a garden shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shed' looks like a garden shed, the second of two places, but it is the verb meaning to cast off.
explanation.definitionFit: A tract is a short religious or political pamphlet handed out to spread a message.

clue.text: Stop redhead getting sort of ice cream

blocks.note: to stem a flow is to stop it
Ginger is a nickname for a red-haired person

explanation.surface: Someone tries to stop a red-haired child getting an ice cream.
explanation.definitionFit: Stem ginger is preserved ginger root in syrup, a popular flavour of ice cream.

clue.text: Large country house of style announced

indicators.note: something announced is spoken out, so the word for style is heard rather than spelt

blocks.note: style or way of doing something

explanation.surface: An estate agent advertises a stately home with real style.
explanation.definitionFit: A manor is the main dwelling of a landed estate, traditionally the lord's residence in the countryside.

clue.text: Audit partner in defeat on board

blocks.note: to audit accounts is to check them
a mate is a partner or companion

explanation.surface: An accountant's partner suffers a loss while auditing the books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' means on a chessboard, not on a company board, which the audit suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: The position ending a chess game, with the king trapped, is the losing player's final defeat.

clue.text: African rhino with one piercing hack butchered

indicators.note: piercing means going into, so these letters are pushed inside the rest
something butchered is chopped up, so its letters are cut and rearranged

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for with
a means one
taken as written

explanation.surface: An African rhinoceros is butchered by poachers with a hacking blade.
explanation.walkthrough: Rhino is old British slang for money, so 'African rhino' is African currency, not the animal. The kwacha is the currency of Zambia and Malawi.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhino is slang for money, and the kwacha is the money of Zambia and Malawi.

clue.text: Cover beginning to appear out of date

indicators.note: the one letter A is asked to move up and appear at the start of the word

blocks.note: declining, fading from fashion

explanation.surface: A shelter starts to look dated.
explanation.walkthrough: Only one letter moves: take the word for declining and bring its A, the first letter of 'appear', to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: An awning is a canvas sheet stretched over a shopfront or window, giving shelter from sun and rain.

clue.text: Tabloid’s name for rabble

blocks.note: a rag is a disparaging word for a cheap newspaper
a tag is a name or label

explanation.surface: A tabloid newspaper coins a sneering nickname for a crowd of protesters.
explanation.definitionFit: A ragtag mob is a disorderly, motley crowd of people, just like a rabble.

clue.text: Dissolute academic lost it in dispute.

indicators.note: what is lost is no longer there, so the little word it is taken out

blocks.note: short for professor
to dispute at law
taken as written

explanation.surface: A professor loses his temper during an argument and behaves badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost it' reads as losing one's temper, but it means remove IT.
explanation.definitionFit: A profligate person lives recklessly and wastefully, given to vice and extravagance.

clue.text: Journey restricted by insubstantial illumination

indicators.note: something restricted is hemmed in, so it is enclosed by the other word

blocks.note: slight means flimsy or insubstantial
a trip is a journey

explanation.surface: A journey is limited by poor lighting.
explanation.definitionFit: A strip light is a long fluorescent tube that provides lighting in offices and kitchens.

clue.text: Verity’s beginning to slip – pity

indicators.note: the start of the word is allowed to slip away, so its first letter goes

blocks.note: verity means truth

explanation.surface: Someone called Verity lets her standards slip, which is a shame.
explanation.walkthrough: Verity looks like a woman's name but is simply the word for truth.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruth is an old word for compassion or sorrow for another, surviving in ruthless, meaning without mercy.

clue.text: Model cited this now, without it and with it

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the following little word is taken away from the letters
to model is to shape or mould, so the letters are moulded into a new form

blocks.note: the twelve letters taken as written
the two letters to remove, taken as written

explanation.surface: A fashion model quoted something as current, then appeared both without it and with it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' looks like a fashion model, but it is the anagram signal; 'without it and with it' plays the deletion against the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Switched on is informal for alert and fashionable, aware of current trends, as is the slang phrase with it.

clue.text: Sort of bags water runs down?

blocks.note: first meaning: bags is British slang for trousers, and this is a narrow style
second meaning: a pipe on a building carrying rainwater away

explanation.walkthrough: Bags is old British slang for trousers; drainpipes are very narrow trousers worn by Teddy boys in the 1950s.
explanation.definitionFit: Drainpipe trousers are tight narrow trousers, and a drainpipe carries rainwater from the roof gutters down.

clue.text: Range of revised airfares those in the centre rejected

indicators.note: the middle letters are thrown out, leaving the outer parts of the word
something revised is reworked, so its letters are put in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written; its two central letters are F and A

explanation.surface: Revised airfares to a mountain region drop the middle tier of prices.
explanation.definitionFit: A sierra is a long jagged chain of mountains, a range, as in Spain or the western United States.

clue.text: This is gained for onset of independence abroad?

definitions.text: This is gained for onset of independence abroad?

indicators.note: the onset is the start, so only the first letter of the next word is used
abroad suggests letters scattered far and wide, rearranged from their order

blocks.note: taken as written
the first letter

explanation.surface: A poor country newly free receives support from overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: help given to a nation abroad may come as it takes its first steps to independence.
explanation.definitionFit: Foreign aid is money or assistance a nation gives to another country, often one starting out independently.

clue.text: Unusual to have two army units side by side

indicators.note: placed next to one another, so the two abbreviations are simply joined end to end

blocks.note: the Royal Artillery, a British army corps
the second of the two units: the Royal Engineers

explanation.surface: It is uncommon for two regiments to fight alongside each other.
explanation.walkthrough: The two units are the Royal Artillery (RA) and Royal Engineers (RE), standard abbreviations of British army corps placed together.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rare seldom occurs or is seldom found, so it is out of the ordinary.

clue.text: One engaged in inept racing? It’s what Ascot could be gripped by

definitions.text: It’s what Ascot could be gripped by

indicators.note: engaged in means involved within, so the letter goes inside the rest
letters racing around are moving wildly, out of their order

blocks.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A clumsy racegoer at Ascot ends up gripped by the action.
explanation.walkthrough: Ascot is not the racecourse but a broad cravat named after it, which a pin holds in place.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiepin is a decorative pin fastening a tie or cravat, such as an ascot, to the shirt.

clue.text: Anger all round, number inside to go blank

indicators.note: the word for anger wraps all the way around what follows
the number sits within the other piece of wordplay

blocks.note: ire is anger
the verb taken as written
N is the abbreviation for number

explanation.surface: An angry person goes blank when a number comes up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blank' looks like an adjective about a blank mind, but here it is the verb: to blank someone is to snub them.
explanation.definitionFit: To blank someone is to snub them deliberately, refusing to acknowledge or notice them at all.

clue.text: China supporting north-eastern country

indicators.note: in a down clue a supporter holds things up from below, so the word for China is placed under the compass direction

blocks.note: the abbreviation for north-east
china plate is rhyming slang for mate, a pal

explanation.surface: China backs a neighbouring country in the north-east.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'supporting' puts the second piece under the first. China is Cockney rhyming slang: china plate means mate.
explanation.definitionFit: Nepal is a Himalayan country lying between India and China, home to Everest.

clue.text: Birmingham’s side overwhelmed by a champion Premier League team

indicators.note: a side is an edge, so only the leading letter of the city is used
something overwhelmed is engulfed, so that letter ends up inside another word

blocks.note: taken as written
a lion is a hero or champion, a celebrated person
the first letter of the city

explanation.surface: A Birmingham football team is crushed by a top Premier League side.
explanation.walkthrough: West Bromwich Albion is a club near Birmingham, so the surface points at the very team the answer names.
explanation.definitionFit: Albion is part of the names of English football clubs, notably West Bromwich Albion and Brighton & Hove Albion.

clue.text: Drunk in Women’s Institute? Certainly not!

blocks.note: the standard abbreviation
a firm refusal

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether there is a drunk in the Women's Institute and is firmly told no.
explanation.walkthrough: The Women's Institute is a respectable British organisation for women, often in villages, known for jam and good works.
explanation.definitionFit: Wino is informal for an alcoholic, especially one who drinks cheap wine on the street.

clue.text: To some extent agency struggled for growth

indicators.note: only partly present, so the letters sit across part of the following words

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: An agency had a hard time trying to grow its business.
explanation.definitionFit: A cyst is an abnormal sac-like swelling in the body, a kind of growth.

clue.text: Attractive part of game for those in the field

definitions.text: part of game for those in the field

blocks.note: first meaning: pleasing, charming

blocks.clueFragment: part of game for those in the field
blocks.note: second meaning: in cricket, the fielders call on the umpire to give a batsman out

explanation.surface: Fielding looks like an attractive part of a game.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the fielding side shouts 'Howzat?' to ask the umpire for a dismissal; that is called appealing.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means charming and pleasant, and also describes cricket fielders asking the umpire for a wicket.

clue.text: John, a sort of councillor

blocks.note: first meaning: slang for a lavatory
second meaning: a member of the monarch's Council in Britain

explanation.walkthrough: John looks like a man's name, but it is the slang word for a toilet. A Privy Counsellor advises the British monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names an old outdoor toilet and also the British sovereign's private advisory council.

clue.text: Fishing tackle Roger put out for these?

definitions.text: Fishing tackle Roger put out for these?

indicators.note: to put out is to eject, so that letter is removed from the word

blocks.note: reels are part of an angler's kit
in radio talk Roger means received, abbreviated R

explanation.surface: An angler called Roger sets out his tackle, hoping to catch something.
explanation.walkthrough: Roger is not a person but the radio word for received, whose abbreviation R comes out; the whole clue then hints at what is being fished for.
explanation.definitionFit: Eels are long snake-like fish that anglers set lines and traps to catch.

clue.text: Subject to chance, back to racing in Asia perhaps

indicators.note: the back of a word is its end, so only the last letter is used
in places that letter within the word for a large landmass

blocks.note: Asia is an example of a continent
the last letter

explanation.surface: A gambler returns to horse racing in the Far East, leaving everything to luck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' marks Asia as only one example of the larger class.
explanation.definitionFit: Contingent describes something that depends on an uncertain event, so its outcome rests on luck.
